street_feel: St Peters Road north of the roundabout is a two-lane road with a thick bundle of wires on wooden poles along the west side (CBC 2018 photo at 154 St Peters Road): gas station, old cedar-shingle houses turned offices right beside it, a small wooden business sign on two posts on the lawn next door. Low, scrappy, half residential.

The Capital Drive / University Avenue power centre is mostly asphalt: BuyMart and The House Depot sit far back behind a lot of 300 by 200 m with nothing in it yet; lot lights and corrals are the cheapest way to make it read as a real lot.

Capital Drive west of North River Road is the hotel-and-drive-through stretch: every business has its own tall pole sign at the road edge, about 7-10 m, a new one every 60-80 m, most with a letter board (VACANCY, tournament welcomes).
Gas stations get their own price sign automatically (README), so no gas pylons are proposed here; they still lack ice freezers and propane cages, which every Island station has out front.
Malpeque Road at Capital Drive is where town turns into the industrial park: church pylon, Countess Auto behind, then Walsh Road with Bent Nail's lumber yard and Mostly Reliable's used lot.
Late November: Christmas trees for sale on lots, pellets and ice melt stacked outside the big boxes, and windshield-washer jugs by every gas station door.

The CBC photo of the St Peters Road / bypass displaced left turn (2020) shows the junction is wide, with red-concrete medians and tall cobra-head lights; a red-roofed commercial building sits on the north-east corner.
